quests.sentence: Our team usually meets on Mondays.
quests.ruleExplanation: Meets is the simple present form, describing the team's regular habit.
quests.nativeTip: This is the normal weekly pattern, not an exception.
quests.example: Our team usually meets on Mondays.

quests.sentence: This week, the team is meeting on Wednesday instead, because of the holiday.
quests.ruleExplanation: Is meeting is the present progressive form, describing a temporary exception to the normal routine.
quests.nativeTip: 'This week' signals a one-time change from the usual pattern.
quests.example: This week, the team is meeting on Wednesday instead, because of the holiday.

quests.sentence: Normally I take the bus, but I'm driving today since my car is finally fixed.
quests.ruleExplanation: Am driving is the present progressive form, describing today's temporary change from the usual habit.
quests.nativeTip: Today is different from the normal pattern described in the first half of the sentence.
quests.example: Normally I take the bus, but I'm driving today since my car is finally fixed.

quests.sentence: The company operates in twelve countries.
quests.ruleExplanation: Operates is the simple present form, describing a permanent characteristic of the company.
quests.nativeTip: This is a lasting fact about the business, not a temporary state.
quests.example: The company operates in twelve countries.

quests.sentence: The company is operating with a reduced staff this month due to renovations.
quests.ruleExplanation: Is operating is the present progressive form, describing a temporary situation rather than a permanent fact.
quests.nativeTip: 'This month' marks a temporary situation with a clear end point.
quests.example: The company is operating with a reduced staff this month due to renovations.

quests.sentence: Our neighbors are being unusually friendly this week.
quests.ruleExplanation: Are being is the present progressive form, describing temporary behavior rather than a lasting personality trait.
quests.nativeTip: This describes behavior limited to this week, not their usual personality.
quests.example: Our neighbors are being unusually friendly this week.

quests.sentence: The toddler keeps knocking over his juice cup at dinner.
quests.ruleExplanation: Keeps is the simple present form, describing a repeated habitual action.
quests.nativeTip: 'Keeps' points to a repeated pattern across many dinners, not one moment.
quests.example: The toddler keeps knocking over his juice cup at dinner.

quests.sentence: The toddler is reaching for the salt shaker again.
quests.ruleExplanation: Is reaching is the present progressive form, describing a single ongoing action in this moment.
quests.nativeTip: This describes one specific action happening right now.
quests.example: The toddler is reaching for the salt shaker again.

quests.sentence: Every time we go out to eat, he insists on ordering pizza.
quests.ruleExplanation: Insists is the simple present form, describing a consistently repeated choice rather than a single event.
quests.nativeTip: 'Every time' signals a pattern that repeats across many occasions.
quests.example: Every time we go out to eat, he insists on ordering pizza.

quests.sentence: The audience was still finding their seats when the orchestra began to play.
quests.ruleExplanation: Was finding is the past progressive form, describing the background action still underway when the orchestra began.
quests.nativeTip: One action was already happening in the background when the main event started.
quests.example: The audience was still finding their seats when the orchestra began to play.

quests.sentence: The orchestra began to play right on schedule.
quests.ruleExplanation: Began is the simple past form, describing the main event as a complete action.
quests.nativeTip: This is the main event itself, treated as one complete action rather than a backdrop.
quests.example: The orchestra began to play right on schedule.

quests.sentence: While the waiter was taking our order, the fire alarm suddenly went off.
quests.ruleExplanation: Was taking is the past progressive form, describing the ongoing background action interrupted by the alarm.
quests.nativeTip: One action was in progress when a sudden event cut through it.
quests.example: While the waiter was taking our order, the fire alarm suddenly went off.

quests.sentence: I usually walk to work, but I'll be driving tomorrow because of the delivery I'm expecting.
quests.ruleExplanation: Will be driving is the future progressive form, describing an action that will be in progress at a specific future time.
quests.nativeTip: Picture tomorrow morning specifically — the driving will already be underway at that point.
quests.example: I usually walk to work, but I'll be driving tomorrow because of the delivery I'm expecting.

quests.sentence: I'll drive to the airport to pick up my parents on Friday.
quests.ruleExplanation: Will drive is the simple future form, describing one complete planned action.
quests.nativeTip: This is a single planned action, not something viewed mid-progress.
quests.example: I'll drive to the airport to pick up my parents on Friday.

quests.sentence: By the time you call, I'll probably be sitting in traffic already.
quests.ruleExplanation: Will be sitting is the future progressive form, describing an action expected to be in progress at that future moment.
quests.nativeTip: One situation will already be underway before the other future action happens.
quests.example: By the time you call, I'll probably be sitting in traffic already.

quests.sentence: The weather forecaster says it rains almost every afternoon in April here.
quests.ruleExplanation: Rains is the simple present form, describing a recurring general truth about the climate.
quests.nativeTip: This describes a general seasonal pattern, not today specifically.
quests.example: The weather forecaster says it rains almost every afternoon in April here.

quests.sentence: It's raining harder than the forecast predicted.
quests.ruleExplanation: Is raining is the present progressive form, describing a specific ongoing weather event.
quests.nativeTip: This describes what's happening outside right now.
quests.example: It's raining harder than the forecast predicted.

quests.sentence: The team usually struggles in the first quarter, but tonight they're leading from the start.
quests.ruleExplanation: Are leading is the present progressive form, describing unusual current behavior that breaks from their normal pattern.
quests.nativeTip: Notice the contrast between their usual pattern and what's happening specifically tonight.
quests.example: The team usually struggles in the first quarter, but tonight they're leading from the start.

quests.sentence: When I was a kid, I collected stamps.
quests.ruleExplanation: Collected is the simple past form, describing a repeated habit within a finished period of time.
quests.nativeTip: This describes a habit that lasted across a completed period of childhood.
quests.example: When I was a kid, I collected stamps.

quests.sentence: I was collecting shells on the beach when the tide started coming in fast.
quests.ruleExplanation: Was collecting is the past progressive form, describing an action in progress at the moment the tide shifted.
quests.nativeTip: One action was already happening when something else changed the situation.
quests.example: I was collecting shells on the beach when the tide started coming in fast.

quests.sentence: Back then, my brother played guitar every weekend, but that summer he was performing at a different venue almost every night.
quests.ruleExplanation: Was performing is the past progressive form, describing an intense temporary period, in contrast with his usual weekend routine.
quests.nativeTip: Focus on the busier, temporary stretch described later in the sentence, not his usual weekend habit.
quests.example: Back then, my brother played guitar every weekend, but that summer he was performing at a different venue almost every night.

quests.sentence: The board will vote on the merger next Thursday.
quests.ruleExplanation: Will vote is the simple future form, describing a single planned future event.
quests.nativeTip: This is one planned action for a specific future day.
quests.example: The board will vote on the merger next Thursday.

quests.sentence: This time next Thursday, the board will be discussing budget cuts instead, according to the new agenda.
quests.ruleExplanation: Will be discussing is the future progressive form, describing an action expected to be in progress at a specific future time.
quests.nativeTip: Picture that exact future moment — the discussion will already be underway.
quests.example: This time next Thursday, the board will be discussing budget cuts instead, according to the new agenda.

quests.sentence: The new hires will shadow senior staff for their first two weeks.
quests.ruleExplanation: Will shadow is the simple future form, describing an entire planned arrangement rather than an action viewed mid-progress.
quests.nativeTip: Even with a duration mentioned, this describes the whole plan as one complete action, not a single in-progress moment.
quests.example: The new hires will shadow senior staff for their first two weeks.

quests.sentence: The lab is running additional tests to confirm the results.
quests.ruleExplanation: Is running is the present progressive form, describing a project currently in progress.
quests.nativeTip: There's no time word here — decide based on whether this is an ongoing project or a routine.
quests.example: The lab is running additional tests to confirm the results.

quests.sentence: The lab ran three rounds of tests last quarter.
quests.ruleExplanation: Ran is the simple past form, describing completed testing that already took place.
quests.nativeTip: This describes completed, sequential work from a finished period.
quests.example: The lab ran three rounds of tests last quarter.

quests.sentence: The lab will run one final test before publishing the findings.
quests.ruleExplanation: Will run is the simple future form, describing one complete planned future action.
quests.nativeTip: This is a single planned step that hasn't happened yet.
quests.example: The lab will run one final test before publishing the findings.

quests.sentence: The committee is reconsidering its original decision after new evidence surfaced.
quests.ruleExplanation: Is reconsidering is the present progressive form, describing a process currently underway.
quests.nativeTip: This is an ongoing process happening now, not a finished or habitual action.
quests.example: The committee is reconsidering its original decision after new evidence surfaced.

quests.sentence: The committee reconsidered similar decisions twice before, always reaching the same conclusion.
quests.ruleExplanation: Reconsidered is the simple past form, describing repeated but finished past events.
quests.nativeTip: These are separate completed instances from the past, not one action still in progress.
quests.example: The committee reconsidered similar decisions twice before, always reaching the same conclusion.

quests.sentence: By next year, the committee will be operating under an entirely new set of guidelines.
quests.ruleExplanation: Will be operating is the future progressive form, describing an ongoing state expected at a future point in time.
quests.nativeTip: Picture the committee's situation during that future period, not a single completed step.
quests.example: By next year, the committee will be operating under an entirely new set of guidelines.
